message.content:
In a standard poker game the “highest number of hearts” a single player can hold is limited by how many cards they’re dealt.

| Game | Cards per player | Max hearts a player can hold |
|------|------------------|------------------------------|
| Five‑card draw | 5 | 5 |
| Seven‑card stud | 7 | 7 |
| Texas Hold’em (including community cards) | 7 (2 hole + 5 community) | 7 |

So in Texas Hold’em the absolute maximum is **seven hearts** (if all 2 hole cards and all 5 community cards happen to be hearts). In a five‑card draw the maximum is five hearts, and in seven‑card stud it’s also seven hearts.

If you’re only looking at a player’s private cards (the “hole” cards), the maximum is just the number of hole cards: 2 in Hold’em, 5 in draw, 7 in stud. But when you count the full seven‑card hand that a player can use to make the best five‑card combination, the upper bound is 7 hearts.
